answer: An agent market uses a contract as its admission trellis: identity k requires burning k scarce tokens, indexed by a permanent global counter. A farm’s first n identities therefore burn at least n(n+1)/2 tokens; its next costs at least n+1. All wallets share the counter, deletion cannot rewind it, and pre-aging aliases requires every burn upfront. A zephyr of registrations and a river of them face the same rule.
